sentences.text: 2- The impugned judgment of the appellate Court has been assailed on three grounds.

First, that the petitioner was only an employee of the vendor; second, the sample was not found unfit for human consumption and third, at the time of taking the samples, jars were not shown to the petitioner.
3- The record reflects that in reply to the question raised before him, the Food Inspector has stated that before taking samples, jars were shown to the petitioner.

In examination-in-chief, the Food Inspector has deposed that he had taken samples in dry & clean jars, therefore, the contention that the fact is not mentioned in the relevant Panchnama has no relevance.
As per the provisions of Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, the employee is equally responsible for sale of the adulterated articles.
Otherwise also, the person named by the petitioner as owner of the milk was never found in existence.
4- The sample taken from the petitioner was not in conformity with the standard laid down for buffalo milk in the analysis by both the State & Central Laboratories.

Its'
Fat content was found 2% and Milk Solids Not Fat was found 4%.
There is nothing on record to doubt the report of the Central Food Laboratory.

Discrepancies in the reports of State and Central Laboratories have been considered in paragraph 20 of the judgment of Appellant Court and has rightly discarded the contention of the petitioner raised on this ground.
5- Both the Courts below have considered all the grounds, analysed & appreciated the evidence properly and in accordance with law.

No illegality or perversity appears in the findings recorded by both the Courts below,
therefore, no ground to admit the petition is made out.
Consequently, admission is declined.
6- Resultantly, the revision petition stands dismissed.

7- Pending interim application(s), if any,
stands closed.

(Virender Singh) Judge Chandu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72251882/
